import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures around homogeneous topological spaces

This file formalizes the notion of a weakly first countable topological space and some conjectures
around those.

*References:*
* [Ar2013] Arhangeliski, Alexandr. "Selected old open problems in general topology."
  Buletinul Academiei de Ştiinţe a Republicii Moldova. Matematica 73.2-3 (2013): 37-46.
  https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
-/

open TopologicalSpace Topology Filter Set
open scoped Cardinal

namespace Homogeneous

/--
A topological space $X$ is called *homogeneous* if for all $x, y \in X$ there is homeomorphism
$f : X \to X$ with $f(x) = y$.
-/
class HomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  exists_equiv : ∀ x y : X, ∃ f : X ≃ₜ X, f x = y

/-- Every discrete space is homogeneous. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance DiscreteTopology.toHomogeneousSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [DiscreteTopology X] :
    HomogeneousSpace X where
  exists_equiv x y := by
    classical
    use IsHomeomorph.homeomorph (Equiv.swap x y)
      (IsHomeomorph.equiv_of_discreteTopology (Equiv.swap x y))
    rw [IsHomeomorph.homeomorph_apply, Equiv.swap_apply_left]

/-- Problem 13 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every infinite homogeneous compact hausdorff
space contains a non-trivial convergent sequence? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_inj_tendsto :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), ¬ Finite X → T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → ∃ s : ℕ → X, s.Injective ∧ ∃ a : X, Tendsto s atTop (nhds a) := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 14 in [Ar2013]:
Is it possible to represent an arbitrary compact hausdorff space as an image
of a homogeneous compact space under a continuous mapping? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem homogeneousSpace_exists_surjective :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      ∃ (Y : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace Y), T2Space Y ∧ CompactSpace Y ∧ HomogeneousSpace Y ∧
        ∃ f : Y → X, Continuous f ∧ f.Surjective := by
  sorry

/-- A topological space is called ω-monolithic if
the closure of every countable subspace is metrizable. -/
class CountablyMonolithicSpace (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] : Prop where
  metrizable_of_closure_of_countable : ∀ ⦃s : Set X⦄, s.Countable → MetrizableSpace (closure s)

/-- Every Metrizable space is ω-monolithic. -/
@[category test, AMS 54]
instance MetrizableSpace.countablyMonolithicSpace
    (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [MetrizableSpace X] : CountablyMonolithicSpace X := by
  refine { metrizable_of_closure_of_countable := ?_ }
  intros
  infer_instance

/-- Problem 15 in [Ar2013]:
Is every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space first countable? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem firstCountableTopology_of_countablyMonolithicSpace :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → FirstCountableTopology X := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 16 in [Ar2013]:
Is the cardinality of every homogeneous ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space not greater than 𝔠? -/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_card_lt :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      HomogeneousSpace X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → #X ≤ 𝔠 := by
  sorry

/-- Problem 17 in [Ar2013]:
Is it true that every nonempty ω-monolithic compact hausdorff space contains a point with a
first countable neighborhood basis?

Note: `Nonempty X` is required since the conclusion asserts the existence of a point.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 54]
theorem countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (X : Type) (_ : TopologicalSpace X), T2Space X → CompactSpace X →
      Nonempty X → CountablyMonolithicSpace X → ∃ x : X, (𝓝 x).IsCountablyGenerated := by
  sorry

end Homogeneous

findings.description: Problem 17 assumes monolithicity, but lines 108–110 assume only CountablyMonolithicSpace X. That class checks metrizability of closures of countable subsets. Full monolithicity of a compact Hausdorff space requires w(closure A) ≤ max(ℵ₀, |A|) for every subset A, including uncountable ones. Thus the Lean statement drops the uncountable-subset requirements and asks the stronger ω-monolithic question instead of the cited Problem 17. Its docstring makes the same substitution.
findings.source_evidence: Arhangel’skii, Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology (2013), p. 43, Problem 17: “Is it true that every nonempty monolithic compact space is first-countable at some point?” In contrast, Problems 15 and 16 explicitly say “ω-monolithic.” https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf . The meaning of full monolithicity is confirmed by Arhangel’skii–van Mill, Topological Homogeneity (2014), §11, p. 36: “the weight of the closure of an arbitrary subset A of X does not exceed the cardinality of A.” https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/j.vanmill/papers/papers2014/ArhangMillRecentProgressIII.pdf
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a separate full-monolithicity predicate and use it in Problem 17, leaving CountablyMonolithicSpace unchanged for Problems 15–16. In the compact Hausdorff setting, the required predicate can be written as `∀ s : Set X, ∃ B : Set (Set (closure s)), IsTopologicalBasis B ∧ #B ≤ max ℵ₀ #s`. Change Problem 17’s docstring to say “monolithic,” not “ω-monolithic.” The current stronger question could instead be retained as a separately sourced variant.

findings.description: The module description at lines 22–23 says the file formalizes weak first countability. It actually defines homogeneity and ω-monolithicity; no weak-first-countability definition or problem occurs in this file.
findings.source_evidence: The cited 2013 paper treats weak first countability separately in §3, pp. 38–39. This file’s Problems 13–17 are from §6, “Homogeneous compacta,” pp. 42–43. https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the copied module description with a description of homogeneity, monolithicity, and the associated compact-space problems.

reformulations.difference: Lean asks for an injective convergent sequence, whereas the source asks for a non-trivial convergent sequence. Lean also permits the limit to occur as one term.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: In a T₁ space a convergent sequence with finite range is eventually constant, so a non-eventually-constant convergent sequence has infinite range. Choose distinct values from that range and preimage indices. The indices are injective natural numbers and therefore tend to infinity, so the selected sequence still converges. Conversely, an injective sequence cannot be eventually constant. If its limit occurs among its terms, removing the finite prefix through that term gives an injective sequence avoiding the limit. These equivalences were proved without using the admitted conjecture.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion uses `(𝓝 x).IsCountablyGenerated` rather than explicitly saying that the space is first-countable at x. This concerns only the conclusion, not the incorrect premise reported above.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A countably generated neighborhood filter admits a countable local basis consisting of open neighborhoods; conversely, a countable open local basis generates the neighborhood filter. The pointwise equivalence with `∃ U : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, x ∈ U n ∧ IsOpen (U n)) ∧ ∀ V ∈ 𝓝 x, ∃ n, U n ⊆ V` was proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: A. V. Arhangel’skii, Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology (2013), pp. 37–46, especially the standing convention on p. 38 and §6: https://www.math.md/files/basm/y2013-n2-3/y2013-n2-3-(pp37-46).pdf.pdf
A. V. Arhangel’skii and J. van Mill, Topological Homogeneity (2014), especially §§1–3 and §11: https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/j.vanmill/papers/papers2014/ArhangMillRecentProgressIII.pdf
Publisher preview and bibliography for Topological Homogeneity (2014): https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.2991/978-94-6239-024-9_1

A. V. Arhangel’skii, Topological homogeneity. Topological groups and their continuous images (1987), abstract and contents only; full text was unavailable: https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1070/RM1987v042n02ABEH001333/pdf

A. V. Arhangel’skii, Precalibers, monolithic spaces, first countability, and homogeneity in the class of compact spaces (2008), bibliographic metadata only: https://api.elsevier.com/content/article/PII:S0166864108000540?httpAccept=text/xml
G. Plebanek, Monolithic spaces of measures, arXiv:1912.13297v3, introduction and related results: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1912.13297v3

J. Kąkol, O. Kurka and W. Śliwa, The two-disjoint-copies property for compact spaces, homogeneity and connection with Cp-theory, arXiv:2606.27568v1, relevant homogeneity and convergent-sequence passages: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2606.27568v1
Jan van Mill’s homepage and publication list, used to locate the survey: https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/j.vanmill/ ; https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/j.vanmill/papers/papersna1999.html

review.notes: Checked all nine mathematical declarations, the answer scopes, and the relevant Mathlib/FC definitions. Problems 13–16 and both test instances match their intended claims. CompactSpace together with T2Space correctly implements the paper’s standing compact-Hausdorff convention. The consolidated /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles and includes finite/empty boundary tests, Cantor-space witnesses satisfying the joint hypotheses, sequence and neighborhood-basis equivalences, and a proof that full monolithicity implies the existing countable condition for compact Hausdorff spaces. No status mismatch was established by the sources read. The reviewed file is unchanged.

submission.summary: Added a separate MonolithicSpace predicate imposing the cardinality bound on bases of closures of all subsets, and used it in Problem 17 instead of CountablyMonolithicSpace. Corrected Problem 17’s docstring and the copied module description; other declarations remain unchanged. The file compiles with only `sorry` warnings, and scratch checks verify finite cases and the implication from full monolithicity to ω-monolithicity for compact Hausdorff spaces.

  sorry

/-- A compact Hausdorff space is called *monolithic* if the closure of every subset $s$
has a topological basis of cardinality at most $\max(\aleph_0, |s|)$. -/

  exists_basis_closure : ∀ s : Set X, ∃ B : Set (Set (closure s)),
    IsTopologicalBasis B ∧ #B ≤ max ℵ₀ #s
